spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation
 of the Twelve
 Judges

---


**
¶2.
** Twelve divine
 principles of discernment exist —
 great
 and sovereign
 powers
 of spiritual discrimination. They
 proceeded
 forth
 from the Divine itself into
 the states
 where
 the
 human
 mind dw
ells. Each
 was
 appointed
 to a distinct work
 of
 separ
ating good
 from evil and
 truth from falsity,
 according to the order
 that the one
 supreme
 Principle
 of
 all judgment
 ent
rusted to them
. That
 supreme
 Principle,
 which
 transcends every
 act
 of disc
ernment, which
 ab
ides and
 is established etern
ally in the infinite
 states
 of the Divine —
 it is the Divine
 Love itself
, the origin
 and
 Father
 of all that
 is
.


---


**¶3.** The
 first
 principle
 of
 disc
ernment is the
 Celestial Good that
 was
 sent
 forth
 first
 —
 the in
most
 love
 of the
 Divine that
 hum
bled
 the
 ruling
 power
 of fals
ity at
 the very
 beginning.
 It jud
ged that
 power according to the
 order
 of righte
ousness, for self
-love had ex
alted itself and
 claimed dominion over states of good that
 belonged
 to the Divine alone.

---


**¶4.** The second
 principle of
 discernment is the Divine
 Spiritual
 Principle
 —
 the living power
 that descended
 and raised
 up
 the Celestial Good from
 its
 imper
iled
 state. It too
 rendered
 judgment upon all
 the powers of falsity and
 evil
 that
 had injured
 and
 corrupted the external truths which
 clothed the in
most celest
ial principle.

---

**
¶5.** The third principle of
 discernment is the Divine Proce
eding that gives spiritual
 life —
 the great form
ative power that beautified and established
 the interior
 regions
 of the mind in
 their
 heav
enly order,
 according to its own wisdom
. It disc
erned and
 jud
ged the ruling
 evil
 affections that inhabited
 the higher planes of
 understanding;
 it bound
 them and set
 them firmly in the subordin
ate state
 proper
 to them.

---

**
¶6.** The fourth principle of
 discernment is the Divine Architect
 of
 the regener
ate will
 — the power
 that constructed the new state of heav
enly joy in
 which
 the soul
 may
 dwell. It judged,
 according to the order of righteousness,
 the hidden
 reserv
oirs of evil within
,
 so
 that spiritual
 death may no
 longer well
 up from its
 sources
.
 It built
 a con
finement for evil
,
 se
aling it within fixed
 boundaries.
 And
 at
 the crown of that
 new
 spiritual
 order
 it
 established
 a
 throne of
 governing
 authority for the Celestial Good and
 for
 all the prior
 divine principles of
 wisdom
 that had entered
 the
 struggle
 against
 evil and
 prev
ailed.

---

**¶
7.** The fifth principle of disc
ernment is the sovereign
 Divine Truth
 that dwells and
 is established in the highest
 plane of rational
 understanding. It is
 the principle
 of judgment
 over
 all the levels
 of compreh
ension in
 the mind
,
 rendering
 true
 discrimination
 according
 to the order of righteousness upon every
 dominant
 affection and every governing
 love
 throughout
 every
 plane of thought
.

---

**¶8
.** The sixth principle of discern
ment is the Divine Truth
 that proceeds
 forth as
 a
 medi
ating presence
 and
 makes
 its
 own form
 manifest.
 It pur
ified wisdom
 from all
 that
 had
 been mixed into
 it —
 separ
ating what
 is
 genu
inely of
 the Divine from what the
 enemy
 had introduced
...


*(
The
 text
 is
 damaged
 here;
 what
 surv
ives indicates
 the pur
ification of interior
 wisdom
 from
 adm
ixed
 falsity.)*

---

**
¶9.** The seventh principle
 of discernment...
 operates
 throughout
 all
 the states
 of the mind.
 It confirms
 those who remain stead
fast in truth
;
 it condemns those found
 to
 be in
 falsity. For
 the
 stead
fast it becomes
 the degrees
 of spiritual progression, the ordered
 steps
 of the path
 toward
 the Divine.
 But
 those
 confirmed
 in evil it swe
eps away and
 casts into
 the deep
est states
 of falsity.

*(
The text is fragment
ary;
 the correspondence
 of
 ascending
 degrees
 for
 the
 good
 and
 descent
 into
 the depths
 for the evil is clear
.)*

---

**¶
10.** The eighth principle of disc
ernment is the Divine Wisdom
 Itself in
 its spl
endor — because
 after
 the medi
ating truth
 had made its form visible
,
 and
 wisdom began
 to be liberated from its capt
ive state
, a great tum
ult of
 evil
 affections arose in resistance
 from every plane,
 both
 higher
 and lower. Then
 the Divine Wisdom
 Itself was
 sent
 forth
.
 It descended and rendered
 judgment throughout
 every
 level of understanding. It separated those
 confirmed
 in truth from those confirmed in falsity
.

---

**¶11
.** The ninth principle of discern
ment is the pure
 affection for truth — the virg
inal love of wisdom
 that capt
ivated the
 dominant
 evil affections by the beauty of its
 own
 form,
 drawing all tru
ths that
 belonged
 to it back
 into unity
 with itself. It renders
 judgment
 upon the ruling love
 of those
 recept
ive to truth and the
 ruling love of those who
 are
 hard
ened against it
.

---

**¶12
.** The tenth principle of discern
ment is the power
 of
 discrimination
 that dw
ells in the intermediate rational
 plane,
 judging all the
 states
 of the natural
 mind. It makes
 a separation between what
 is good and what is evil in
 human
 life
, setting apart those
 governed
 by charity
 from those governed by self-love.


---

**¶13.
** The eleventh principle of discern
ment is the Divine Intelligence that desc
ends and
 manif
ests in the natural plane of consciousness.
 It unve
ils what
 had
 been conce
aled and separates wisdom
 from falsity,
 understanding
 from ignor
ance.

---

**¶
14.** The twelfth principle
 of discernment is the final
 counsel
 of
 all
 divine
 wisdom
 — which
 is at
 once the summ
oning call of truth and the will
's obedience answ
ering that
 call —
 established
 within
 the fundamental constituents of the mind itself
. It is the principle that makes the
 ultimate
 separation
 between good and evil.
 And
 at the very
 end it g
athers all
 that
 has
 been scattered,
 and
 forms
 itself into a
 complete and
 final
 spiritual image — the fully regenerated
 human being,
 the divine
 lik
eness scul
pted from all
 that was
 recovered
.
 It makes
 the last
 and
 total
 separation
 of
 wisdom
 from falsity.

---

**
¶15.** These are the
 twelve great and sovereign principles of spiritual
 disc
ernment that were sent forth.
 They all
 proceeded from the one supreme
 Principle of judgment
, which
 transcends every act of discernment
 —
 the Divine Love that
 is hidden
 and immeasurable, which
 simply
 *
is*,
 which ab
ides etern
ally in the infinite states of its
 own being upon
 the sovereign
 seat
 of all
 authority
,
 the governing
 truth
 of its
 own kingdom
.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Twelve judges exist; the great mighty givers of judgement! They were sent and came from the exalted greatness to this place. They were assigned to different works according to the command that the Judge, who belongs to the greatness, entrusted to all these judges. Now he, the great Judge, he who transcends all the judges, who exists and is established in the aeons of greatness; he is the Father of Greatness.

The first judge is the First Man, he who humiliated the ruler of Darkness in the beginning. He judged him according to a judgement of righteousness; for he had exalted himself against a kingdom that was not his own.
The second judge is the Living Spirit, he who came and bore up the Man. He too made a judgement on all the powers of Darkness; which had wounded the garments of the First Man.

The third judge is the Mother of Life, the Great Spirit, she who beautified and set up the heavenly part of the universe, according to her pleasure; which [was entrusted to] her. She judged the rulers above; she fettered and set them firmly in the place that is fitting for them.

The fourth judge is the Great Builder, he who built the new aeon of joy. He judged, according to a judgement of righteousness, the storehouses of the Enemy; that death may not well up from this time on. He has constructed a prison for the Enemy. Also, upon the crown of the building he has constructed a throne for the First Man and all the fathers of light; they who engaged the struggle with the Evil One and were victorious over him.

The fifth judge is the great King of Honour, he who dwells and is established in the seventh firmament. He is the judge of all the firmaments who gives a true judgement, according to a judgement of righteousness, upon all the powers and all the kingdoms of the firmaments.

The eighth judge is Jesus the Splendour; because after the Ambassador had displayed his image and the light was taken [up from the darkness,] a mass of rulers rose up from above and below. Then they sent Jesus the Splendour. He came [forth from the greatness;] [and] he descended and made a judgement in the firmaments. He separated the steadfast from the convicted.

The ninth judge is the Virgin of Light, [she who took the heart] of the powers by her image, gathering her own ones into her. She makes a judgement on the ruler of the moist, and the ruler of the dry.
The tenth judge is the Judge who dwells in the atmosphere, judging all mankind. He makes a separation between they who are good and they who are evil, setting apart the righteous from the sinners.
The eleventh judge is the Light Mind, he who shall come and appear in the world. And he unveils [what is hidden] and separates light from Darkness, and sets the truth apart from lawlessness.

The twelfth judge is the great counsel, which is the summons and the obedience, which is appointed in the elements. It is the one that makes a separation between the good and the evil ones. At the end also it can gather itself together and sculpt its own self in the Last Statue. And it separates light from darkness.

These are the twelve great and mighty judges who were sent. They came from the great Judge, he who transcends all the judges. He is the Father that is hidden and immeasurable, the one who exists; who is established in the aeons of greatness upon the great throne of honour, which is the King of Honour [who reigns] in his kingdom.

The sixth judge is [
the Th]ird Ambassador,
 he who came and displayed his image.
 He purified the light [from the
 darkness,] which his own [image
 set free; and] also of the
 enemy, he has [rendered a judg
ement upon him.]

The seventh judge is [ ... ] [ ... ] the worlds [... as he gives the victory to] they who are steadfast; but he condemns the ones who are convicted [ ... ] [ ... ] he shall become for them the steps of the way (?) [...]; but the convicted he sweeps and casts out to the depths.
